loggerFailure: Every helper catches ordinary JS exceptions, attempts one bounded logger-error if space/stdout permit, stops further records. A failed stdout may prevent that error record too; absence cannot pass. Uncatchable engine/host traps are not promised catchable.

adapter.token: Separate component-local counter held in handleResources local completionTrace across existing awaits; never current-global
adapter.bytes: readBytes/readChunks count chunks returned by existing reader; not successfully written/peer-received bytes. EOF only when existing part.done branch is taken; a no-body response has no fabricated EOF.

postCleanupFlags.2: cleanupReturned as computed by original finally

adapter.normalReturnSite: Immediately after original primary/fatal guards, with no new return/await. Can be reached on original accepted handled-closed path, not only normal finished-body path; no public Promise-settled or host-quiescence claim.

childHandlerPromise.fulfilled: Emitted after the explicit await of this internal handler.handle call fulfills. Its fulfillment value is returned unchanged and is never serialized.
childHandlerPromise.rejected: The original caught reason is rethrown unchanged, including undefined/null/false/0/emptystring. Only typeof/null is logged. The catch covers invocation failure or await rejection and does not by itself prove that a Promise object had been returned. No disposal is performed by this catch.
childHandlerPromise.sourceLocalAssociation: A plain holder is allocated per neutral invocation inside its existing preparation/pre-entry catch. handle receives it as a third INTERNAL JavaScript argument, captures it in its runFreshRequest callback closure, and handleResources assigns the actual adapter trace after Request/trace creation. This shares the actual trace object reference, not a correlation of IncomingMessage and Request by equality/order.
childHandlerPromise.nativeApi: runFreshRequest retains its original callback/receiver/incoming/outparam arguments. No extra native/WIT parameter, slot, AsyncLocalStorage API or ABI export.
childHandlerPromise.missingTrace: No child marker is fabricated if trace assignment was not reached, the route was unselected, or the logger stopped. Absence remains unobserved.

classic.token: Independent component-local counter at synchronous genuine requestHandler wrapper, never assumed equal to adapter token
classic.handler: Return requestHandler(req,res) directly, no await. Only public once finish/close observers; no error listener or new HTTP handler/endpoint.

correlation.sequenceScope: Component-local emission-attempt sequence only; counters reset from snapshot and can collide/interleave across component instances in one stdout
correlation.rule: Never concatenate equal numeric tokens across instances/lanes or infer identity from method/path/order. Missing/truncated/logger-error/colliding/interleaved-ambiguous traces remain unobserved. Only an unambiguous adapter lane trace can support its own readEOF→dispose-return→finish-return order; no unique outer↔inner causal join.
correlation.actualReferenceScope: Child-handler sites use holder.trace, the same Source-local object reference as the adapter invocation. This is explicit internal JavaScript reference flow, not an inferred numeric join. Raw logs still contain only colliding component-local numbers and cannot authenticate cross-instance physical handles or classic-lane joins.

interpretation: Explicit adapter-catch is evidence of a guest-observed exception at the recorded existing phase. Keep native primary/falsy-error/cancel/disposal semantics unchanged.
A finish-return marker proves that the imported public OutgoingBody.finish call returned at that site, not a private finish-call count, hostTCP EOF, browser completion or resource retirement.

Finish-return precedes original finally and final guards. Post-cleanup only proves that original finally reached its end and records primarySet/cleanupReturned; original releaseInput or another uncaught cleanup exception can bypass this marker. Missing is unobserved. Normal-return-site records fallthrough after both unchanged guards, not Promise settlement, export-return observation or host quiescence.
A complete unambiguous adapter trace plus browser abort locates a public completion disagreement; it does not prove browser-only cause or exclude host transport behavior.
Public classic finish/close is lane-local. GET/action-result can be an independently handled route and is not identified as a particular POST self-fetch by equality/path/order.
No normal marker, missing lane or lost log is not proof that native append, fetch EOF or private cleanup failed.
A child-handler-promise-fulfilled record follows the ONE explicit await of internal handler.handle; it does not observe the enclosing neutral callback or generated/native export settling.
The new rejection catch logs then rethrows the exact reason; it does not enter the preparation-disposal catch or perform resource disposal. Existing logger ordinary-exception handling remains.
All inherited and new records use NEXT_GUEST_PROMISE_COMPLETION_V1, avoiding confusion with held response-only generation logs.

entryReplacements.before: // Pure orchestration, inlined unchanged into each raw guest entry.
entryReplacements.after: // Neutral orchestration with one explicit child-handler Promise await; no extra resource disposal.

perturbation: ONE explicit code await is added at the prior return handler.handle boundary for every neutral invocation. It changes Promise reaction/adoption scheduling; child site emissions remain conditional on the selected adapter trace. Per-invocation object allocation and new stdout calls also perturb timing. No fix/reliability, fulfilled whole export, native return or host completion claim.
readinessOwnership: Holder allocation remains inside the original readiness/pre-entry catch, before handler ownership. The new await and rejection log are in a separate later try/catch, with no duplicate pre-entry disposal after ownership. Existing handle pre-entry cleanup, adapter catch/finally and final guards are untouched.
